dialogueBeats.shotDescription: GINA. TRUDY typing the report with two fingers and a coffee. GINA at a desk with a sling and a telephone, answering a board she can't reach.

captions.text:
GINA: Seventy-one pages and none of them
say what happened.

dialogueBeats.shotDescription: CASTILLO alone above the city with the ledgers in a file under his arm. He looks at Miami the way a man looks at a thing he has agreed to keep.
The black convertible going east into the light, top down, hazard lights ticking, the way the truck did at the beginning.
Crockett on the sand in his shoes, fully dressed, watching the water come up and go back out. Nobody with him.
The board wiped. TRUDY writes a new name on it. The telephone rings and somebody answers it.
Sun on the blue crates, which are still there, stacked, waiting for somebody else's paperwork.

captions.text: [Gulls; a distant forklift.]

dialogueBeats.shotDescription: A small service. LUPE puts a photocopy of her father's numbers on the grave and weights it with a stone, so it won't blow away.
The ST. VITUS leaves her slip with Crockett at the wheel and nobody else aboard.

captions.text: [A diesel engine; rigging; gulls.]

dialogueBeats.shotDescription: The boat well out, the city small and white behind it, the water doing what water does.
A radio crackles. Crockett looks at it for a moment before he answers.

dialogueBeats.text: Go ahead.
dialogueBeats.shotDescription: CROCKETT (into the radio). A radio crackles. Crockett looks at it for a moment before he answers.

captions.text: CROCKETT: Go ahead.

dialogueBeats.text: Boat. We've got one on the river.
dialogueBeats.shotDescription: DISPATCH (O.S.). A radio crackles. Crockett looks at it for a moment before he answers.

captions.text:
DISPATCH (O.S.): Boat. We've got one on
the river.

dialogueBeats.shotDescription: He looks back at the city once, and then he turns the wheel and takes it.
